lem-general-linear-quotient-stacks-are-a:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $X$ be an affine finite-type
$\mathbb C$-scheme with an algebraic action of
$G=\prod_{r=1}^m\operatorname{GL}_{n_r,\mathbb C}$, allowing $n_r=0$.
Then the quotient stack $[X/G]$, defined by $G$-torsors with equivariant
maps to $X$, is an algebraic stack. The morphism $X\to[X/G]$ from the
trivial torsor is a smooth surjective representable atlas, and the diagonal
of $[X/G]$ is representable by affine schemes.
def-quiver-representation-stacks-and-exa:
## Definition

Let $Q=(Q_0,Q_1,s,t)$ be a finite quiver, in the convention of
[[def-path-ring-of-a-finite-quiver-over-the-integers]], and work over
$\mathbb C$. A **dimension vector** is a function
$\mathbf d:Q_0\to\mathbb Z_{\ge0}$. Put
$
V_i^{\mathbf d}=\mathbb C^{d_i},\qquad
\operatorname{Rep}_Q(\mathbf d)=
\bigoplus_{h:i\to j}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb C}
(V_i^{\mathbf d},V_j^{\mathbf d}),\qquad
G_{\mathbf d}=\prod_{i\in Q_0}\operatorname{GL}(V_i^{\mathbf d}).
$
The group acts by change of basis:
$(g\cdot X)_h=g_jX_hg_i^{-1}$. The **representation stack**
$\mathfrak M_{\mathbf d}=[\operatorname{Rep}_Q(\mathbf d)/G_{\mathbf d}]$
is the quotient stack: over a scheme $T$, its objects are left
$G_{\mathbf d}$-torsors $P\to T$ with equivariant maps
$P\to\operatorname{Rep}_Q(\mathbf d)$;
arrows are equivariant isomorphisms commuting with these maps. The
finite-dimensional atlas and the algebraic-stack conditions are verified in
[[lem-general-linear-quotient-stacks-are-algebraic]].

For two dimension vectors $\mathbf a,\mathbf b$, write
$\mathbf d=\mathbf a+\mathbf b$ and choose
$V_i^{\mathbf d}=V_i^{\mathbf a}\oplus V_i^{\mathbf b}$. Let
$\operatorname{Rep}_Q(\mathbf a,\mathbf b)$ be the vector space of
representations preserving $V^{\mathbf a}$. For an arrow $h:i\to j$, its
matrix has the form
$
X_h=
\begin{pmatrix}
X_h^{\mathbf a}&C_h\\
0&X_h^{\mathbf b}
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad C_h\in\operatorname{Hom}(V_i^{\mathbf b},V_j^{\mathbf a}).
$
Let $P_{\mathbf a,\mathbf b}\subseteq G_{\mathbf d}$ be the subgroup preserving
the chosen graded subspaces. Define the **exact-sequence stack**
$
\mathfrak E_{\mathbf a,\mathbf b}
=[\operatorname{Rep}_Q(\mathbf a,\mathbf b)/P_{\mathbf a,\mathbf b}].
$
Its maps are
$
\mathfrak M_{\mathbf a}\times\mathfrak M_{\mathbf b}
\xleftarrow{\ q\ }\mathfrak E_{\mathbf a,\mathbf b}
\xrightarrow{\ p\ }\mathfrak M_{\mathbf d}.
$
The map $q$ sends an exact sequence to its subrepresentation and quotient;
$p$ forgets the subrepresentation. Thus the order convention is
$0\to M_{\mathbf a}\to M_{\mathbf d}\to M_{\mathbf b}\to0$.
The block form shows that the off-diagonal extension parameters are the
coordinates $C_h$; it does not assert that extension classes are a vector
space after quotienting by automorphisms.

~~~tikzcd
\mathfrak M_{\mathbf a}\times\mathfrak M_{\mathbf b}
& \mathfrak E_{\mathbf a,\mathbf b}
  \arrow[l,"q"'] \arrow[r,"p"]
& \mathfrak M_{\mathbf a+\mathbf b}
~~~

The diagram records only the two maps just defined; it supplies no equality of
maps or algebraic operation by itself.
lem-quiver-exact-sequence-correspondence:
## Statement

Assume AC. Let $Q$ be a finite quiver and let $\mathbf a,\mathbf b$ be
dimension vectors. In the notation of
[[def-quiver-representation-stacks-and-exact-sequence-correspondences]], the
map $q:\mathfrak E_{\mathbf a,\mathbf b}\to
\mathfrak M_{\mathbf a}\times\mathfrak M_{\mathbf b}$ is a smooth morphism of
algebraic stacks of relative complex dimension
$
r_Q(\mathbf a,\mathbf b)
=\sum_{h:i\to j} b_i a_j-\sum_{i\in Q_0}a_i b_i
=-\chi_Q(\mathbf b,\mathbf a),
$
where
$
\chi_Q(\mathbf u,\mathbf v)
=\sum_i u_i v_i-\sum_{h:i\to j}u_i v_j.
$
The forgetful map $p:\mathfrak E_{\mathbf a,\mathbf b}\to
\mathfrak M_{\mathbf a+\mathbf b}$ is representable and proper. These claims
allow loops, multiple arrows, zero coordinates, and the empty quiver.
lem-algebraic-milnor-neighborhoods-admit:
## Statement

Assume AC. Let $X$ be a smooth affine complex variety, $f:X\to\mathbb C$ regular, $p\in f^{-1}(0)$, and $\mathcal S$ a finite complex algebraic Whitney stratification for which a bounded complex $A$ is constructible. There is a cofinal family of neighborhoods
$$N=X\cap B_\epsilon(a)\cap f^{-1}(T_\delta),\qquad T_\delta=\{z:|\operatorname{Re}z|<\delta,\ |\operatorname{Im}z|<\delta\},$$
with $p\in B_\epsilon(a)$, such that $f$ on the closed-ball model over $T_\delta\setminus\{0\}$ is proper and submersive on every interior and sphere-boundary stratum. It therefore admits continuous controlled stratum-preserving transport over compact base paths, preserving the sphere and its interior. Transport also gives the natural coefficient comparisons for $A$. In particular it applies to paths inside either half-rectangle $\operatorname{Re}z>0$ or $\operatorname{Re}z<0$. Centres $a$ need not equal $p$. The system may instead use circular function discs. For these choices the neighborhood and its positive-half-disc part have finite constructible cochain models, and their relative homology and cohomology are bounded finite-dimensional. Smooth affine charts give the corresponding local assertion on smooth finite-type complex varieties.
def-intrinsic-quotient-stack-borel-moore:
## Definition

Assume AC as inherited from [[def-equivariant-borel-moore-homology-and-correspondence-convolution]]. For a separated finite-type complex variety $X$ with an algebraic action of a finite product $G$ of general linear groups, put $g=\dim_{\mathbb C}G$. The **intrinsic quotient-stack Borel–Moore grading** of this presentation is
$$\mathbb H_i([X/G];\mathbb Q)=H_{i+2g}^{\mathrm{BM},G}(X;\mathbb Q).$$
The group on the right has exactly the variety dualizing normalization of the cited supplier, $\omega_X^G|_X=\omega_X$. Equivalently, for a sufficiently acyclic free general linear frame space $U$ of dimension $t$, the group is the stable value $H_{i+2t}^{\mathrm{BM}}(X\times_GU;\mathbb Q)$ in each fixed degree. There is no one finite approximation asserted to compute all degrees.

For representation stacks use $X=\operatorname{Rep}_Q(\mathbf d)$ and $G=G_{\mathbf d}$ from [[def-quiver-representation-stacks-and-exact-sequence-correspondences]]. For an extension or flag presentation $[Y/P]$ with total-dimension group $G$ and block parabolic $P$, use the induced variety $S=G\times_PY$ and set $\mathbb H_i([Y/P])=H_{i+2\dim G}^{\mathrm{BM},G}(S)$. The induction and frame comparisons for these presentations are proved in [[lem-quiver-parabolic-levi-borel-model-comparisons]]; this formula does not assert presentation independence for arbitrary Artin stacks.

If $X$ is smooth of dimension $x$, write $D=x-g$. Then $\mathbb H_i([X/G])=H_G^{2D-i}(X;\mathbb Q)$. The complex orientation, rational coefficients and the intrinsic shift are part of this convention. No Tate enrichment is included. Rank-zero general linear factors are omitted and the empty product is the trivial group.
def-quiver-potential-and-monodromic-vani:
## Definition

Assume AC as inherited from the equivariant constructible category. Let $Q$
be a finite complex quiver. A **potential** is a finite $\mathbb C$-linear
combination of directed cycles in $\mathbb C Q$, modulo cyclic rotation.
For $h_1:i_0\to i_1,\ldots,h_\ell:i_{\ell-1}\to i_0$, its trace on a
representation $X$ is $\operatorname{tr}(X_{h_\ell}\cdots X_{h_1})$.
Extending linearly defines the invariant regular function $W_{\mathbf d}$
on $X_{\mathbf d}=\operatorname{Rep}_Q(\mathbf d)$. Its critical locus is
the zero scheme of $dW_{\mathbf d}$.

An **on-shell monodromic homological coefficient datum** consists of the
following. For each dimension vector choose $S_{\mathbf d}\subset\mathbb C$
containing its critical values, with $S_{\mathbf a}+S_{\mathbf b}\subset
S_{\mathbf a+\mathbf b}$. One may take every $S_{\mathbf d}=\mathbb C$.
For every value supply a bounded equivariant constructible complex
$K_{\mathbf d,z}$ on the representation action nerve, supported on
$\operatorname{Crit}(W_{\mathbf d})\cap W_{\mathbf d}^{-1}(z)$, with an
invertible monodromy automorphism. These are PRIMARY HOMOLOGICAL
coefficients in the intrinsic grading of
[[def-intrinsic-quotient-stack-borel-moore-grading]]. They are actual
Cartesian complexes on the indicated quotient presentations; no full
six-functor category on arbitrary Artin stacks is presumed.

For the subobject-first correspondence
$B=\mathfrak M_{\mathbf a}\times\mathfrak M_{\mathbf b}
\xleftarrow q E=\mathfrak E_{\mathbf a,\mathbf b}\xrightarrow p
\mathfrak M_{\mathbf a+\mathbf b}$ and $z=z_1+z_2$, put
$r=-\chi_Q(\mathbf b,\mathbf a)$. Supply a coefficient $K_{E,z_1,z_2}$,
a smooth oriented identification and a proper coefficient morphism
$$q^*(K_{\mathbf a,z_1}\boxtimes K_{\mathbf b,z_2})[2r]\simeq K_{E,z_1,z_2},\qquad Rp_*K_{E,z_1,z_2}\longrightarrow K_{\mathbf a+\mathbf b,z}.$$
Here the smooth operation, including the nonrepresentable map $q$, is
interpreted through the affine-bundle/Levi and induced fixed-group frame
models; the datum includes compatibility with those identifications.
Require these maps to preserve monodromy and external products, to obey
proper composition and proper/smooth Cartesian pasting, and to give the
same identifications on every iterated block flag under the tensor
associator. Require $K_{\mathbf0,0}=\mathbb Q$ and the identity maps in
both endpoint correspondences; dimension-zero coefficients at other
values are zero. These are explicit coherence requirements for an
arbitrary supplied datum, not an existence axiom for vanishing cycles.
They retain arbitrary coherent coefficient complexes. In particular a
choice $\omega\otimes\Phi$ remains admissible whenever its required
operations actually exist; it is not silently identified with $D\Phi$
for arbitrary $\Phi$.

The **standard rational instance** uses the normalized functor of
[[thm-normalized-rational-vanishing-cycles-have-coherent-operations]]:
$$\Phi_{\mathbf d,z}=V_{W_{\mathbf d}-z}\mathbb Q_{X_{\mathbf d}},\qquad K_{\mathbf d,z}=D^{G_{\mathbf d}}_{X_{\mathbf d}}\Phi_{\mathbf d,z}[-2\dim G_{\mathbf d}].$$
The equivariant duality here is VARIETY normalized; the displayed extra
shift is indispensable. The positive-loop automorphism is $T$ on $\Phi$,
and the homological coefficient has contragredient transport $D(T^{-1})$.
For an isolated critical point,
$H^k(\Phi)_x=\widetilde H^{k-1}(F_x;\mathbb Q)$; reduced $H^0$ is in
degree one. This is consistent with $V_0\mathbb Q=\mathbb Q$ and the
unit. For example $x^2$ on $\mathbb A^1$ has its one-dimensional stalk
in degree one, with monodromy $-1$.

On the extension space, Thom–Sebastiani identifies the intrinsic
vanishing cycles of the RESTRICTED trace function with the smooth
pullback of the two diagonal coefficients. Proper functoriality supplies
a morphism from the total-dimension vanishing cycles to the proper
image of that extension coefficient; its dual gives the displayed
homological coefficient morphism. There is no asserted isomorphism to
the inverse image of the total-dimension coefficient. The full standard
realization, its degree and coherent operations are proved in
[[lem-standard-rational-quiver-vanishing-cycles-realize-critical-correspondences]],
recorded in `justified_by`. Mixed Hodge enrichment and off-shell
rapid-decay cohomology are not part of this rational construction.
lem-quiver-parabolic-levi-borel-model-co:
## Statement

Assume AC. Let $G=G_{\mathbf d}$, let $P\subset G$ be a block upper parabolic associated to a finite ordered dimension-vector decomposition, and let $L$ be its block-diagonal Levi. Let $Y$ be the variety of arrow matrices preserving that block flag. The induced spaces $S=G\times_PY$ and $T=G\times_LY$ are separated quasi-projective finite-type complex varieties, with quotient equivalences $[S/G]\simeq[Y/P]$ and $[T/G]\simeq[Y/L]$. With the intrinsic grading of [[def-intrinsic-quotient-stack-borel-moore-grading]], the latter equivalence gives a canonical degree-preserving comparison
$$\mathbb H_*([T/G])\cong\mathbb H_*([Y/L]).$$
It is natural for proper and smooth maps of these induced presentations, compatible with external products, and its comparisons on common product frame models satisfy the cocycle. All assertions include zero block ranks and empty products.
thm-quiver-quotient-stack-borel-moore-op:
## Statement

Assume AC and use the intrinsic rational Borel–Moore grading of [[def-intrinsic-quotient-stack-borel-moore-grading]]. For any finite quiver over $\mathbb C$, the representation, extension and finite block-flag stacks admit the following operations: representable proper invariant-flag-forgetting maps have degree-zero proper pushforward; diagonal-block-forgetting maps have smooth pullback of degree twice their relative stack dimension. For the exact-sequence map $q$ this degree is $2(e-u)=-2\chi_Q(\mathbf b,\mathbf a)$, where $e=\sum_{h:i\to j}b_i a_j$ and $u=\sum_i a_i b_i$.

These operations are independent of the indicated induced-variety and frame presentations, commute with external products, compose with the positive complex orientation, and satisfy proper/smooth base change and Cartesian pasting for the representation/extension/flag diagrams. This includes the two 2-Cartesian squares of three-step quiver flags. Loops, multiple arrows, zero coordinates and the empty quiver are allowed. This statement concerns these particular quotient stacks and maps; it is not a six-functor assertion for arbitrary Artin stacks.
def-untwisted-quiver-cohomological-hall-:
## Definition

Assume AC as inherited from the equivariant Borel–Moore supplier. Let $Q$
be a finite quiver over $\mathbb C$. Use rational equivariant Borel–Moore homology with the positive complex orientation. Its **intrinsic quotient-stack grading** is that of [[def-intrinsic-quotient-stack-borel-moore-grading]]:
$$\mathbb H_i(\mathfrak M_{\mathbf d})=H_{i+2\dim G_{\mathbf d}}^{\mathrm{BM},G_{\mathbf d}}(\operatorname{Rep}_Q(\mathbf d);\mathbb Q).$$
The group on the right uses the variety-normalized dualizing object of [[def-equivariant-borel-moore-homology-and-correspondence-convolution]]; the explicit group-dimension regrading is essential to the shift below. The
untwisted quiver CoHA module is the dimension-vector graded direct sum
$
\mathcal H_Q=\bigoplus_{\mathbf d\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^{Q_0}}
\mathbb H_*(\mathfrak M_{\mathbf d};\mathbb Q).
$
This is an algebraic direct sum; no completion is used.

For $\mathbf a,\mathbf b$, let
$q:\mathfrak E_{\mathbf a,\mathbf b}\to
\mathfrak M_{\mathbf a}\times\mathfrak M_{\mathbf b}$ and
$p:\mathfrak E_{\mathbf a,\mathbf b}\to\mathfrak M_{\mathbf a+\mathbf b}$
be the maps of
[[def-quiver-representation-stacks-and-exact-sequence-correspondences]].
The product of $\alpha$ in dimension $\mathbf a$ and $\beta$ in
dimension $\mathbf b$ is
$
\alpha*\beta:=p_*q^!(\alpha\boxtimes\beta),
$
where $\boxtimes$ is the equivariant external product,
$q^!$ is the smooth complex-oriented Borel–Moore pullback, and $p_*$ is
the proper pushforward. The actual quotient-stack operations and their normalization are proved in
[[thm-quiver-quotient-stack-borel-moore-operation-package]], using the geometry of
[[lem-quiver-exact-sequence-correspondence-is-smooth-and-proper]]. The
homological degree changes by
$
2r_Q(\mathbf a,\mathbf b)=-2\chi_Q(\mathbf b,\mathbf a),
\qquad
\chi_Q(\mathbf u,\mathbf v)=
\sum_i u_i v_i-\sum_{h:i\to j}u_i v_j.
$
Thus the first factor is the subrepresentation and the second is the
quotient. This normalization has no Euler-form sign twist, no division by
automorphism orders, and no additional Tate twist; the coefficient category here is rational constructible sheaves, with no mixed-Hodge enrichment asserted. Each dimension vector has
only finitely many decompositions into $\mathbf a+\mathbf b$, so the product
on the direct sum is defined.

The zero dimension component is $\mathbb Q$; write $1$ for its
standard class, the candidate unit.

The displayed homological shift is for this Borel–Moore normalization and the
subrepresentation-first convention. Under the usual equivariant cohomology
grading, converting through the quotient-stack dimensions gives the source
shift $-2\chi_Q(\mathbf a,\mathbf b)$; it is not obtained by simply
reversing the arguments in the displayed Borel–Moore formula.

**Well-formedness.** The operation package constructs the nonrepresentable smooth pullback through an inverse affine-bundle pullback and a vector-bundle pullback, and the proper pushforward through the induced incidence variety. It proves presentation independence, proper/smooth base change and Cartesian pasting on the needed flag diagrams. Thus the displayed formula is an actual product on the declared intrinsic groups. Associativity and the unit are proved in [[thm-untwisted-quiver-coha-is-associative-and-unital]] rather than assumed here. In each fixed homological degree, a sufficiently large frame model computes the finite collection of operations involved; no single finite model for all degrees is claimed.
lem-quiver-potential-trace-is-additive-o:
## Statement

Let $W$ be a potential of a finite quiver $Q$, and let
$0\to M_{\mathbf a}\to M_{\mathbf a+\mathbf b}\to M_{\mathbf b}\to0$
be represented by a point of the exact-sequence stack. Then
$
W_{\mathbf a+\mathbf b}(M_{\mathbf a+\mathbf b})
=W_{\mathbf a}(M_{\mathbf a})+W_{\mathbf b}(M_{\mathbf b}).
$
thm-untwisted-quiver-coha-is-associative:
## Statement

Assume AC as inherited from the equivariant Borel–Moore and six-functor
suppliers. For every finite quiver $Q$, the multiplication in
[[def-untwisted-quiver-cohomological-hall-algebra]] is associative and has unit
the class $1\in H_0^{\mathrm{BM}}(\operatorname{Rep}_Q(\mathbf 0);\mathbb Q)
=\mathbb Q$.
lem-standard-rational-quiver-vanishing-c:
## Statement

Assume AC. For any finite complex quiver $Q$ and finite potential $W$, put $X_{\mathbf d}=\operatorname{Rep}_Q(\mathbf d)$, $g_{\mathbf d}=\dim G_{\mathbf d}$ and $f_{\mathbf d}=\operatorname{Tr}(W)_{\mathbf d}$. Let $V$ be the normalized rational functor of [[thm-normalized-rational-vanishing-cycles-have-coherent-operations]]. Its coefficients
$$\Phi_{\mathbf d,z}=V_{f_{\mathbf d}-z}\mathbb Q_{X_{\mathbf d}},\qquad K_{\mathbf d,z}=D^{G_{\mathbf d}}_{X_{\mathbf d}}\Phi_{\mathbf d,z}[-2g_{\mathbf d}]$$
are equivariant bounded constructible complexes; $D^G$ has the variety dualizing normalization. With positive monodromy $T$ on $\Phi$, put contragredient transport $D(T^{-1})$ on $K$.

These $K$ give a standard realized instance of the complete generic coefficient datum in [[def-quiver-potential-and-monodromic-vanishing-cycle-data]]. On an extension stack, the proper coefficient map is the dual of
$$\Phi_{\mathbf a+\mathbf b,z}\longrightarrow Rp_*\Psi_{\mathbf a,\mathbf b,z},\qquad \Psi_{\mathbf a,\mathbf b,z}=V_{f_{\mathbf a+\mathbf b}\circ p-z}\mathbb Q.$$
Thom–Sebastiani identifies $\Psi$ on each value-pair summand with $q^*(\Phi_{\mathbf a,z_1}\boxtimes\Phi_{\mathbf b,z_2})$, where $z=z_1+z_2$. It is not an asserted isomorphism to $p^*\Phi_{\mathbf a+\mathbf b,z}$. The realized operations have proper degree zero and smooth degree $-2\chi_Q(\mathbf b,\mathbf a)$, and obey composition, external-product, monodromy, proper/smooth base-change and flag-pasting coherence. This includes loops, multiple arrows, zero coordinates, arbitrary critical values and the empty quiver. For $W=0$ it is precisely the ordinary intrinsic rational Borel–Moore operation package.
def-critical-quiver-coha-from-vanishing-:
## Definition

Assume AC. Let $Q,W$ and an on-shell monodromic homological coefficient
datum $\mathscr K$ be as in
[[def-quiver-potential-and-monodromic-vanishing-cycle-data]]. Define
$$\mathcal H^{\mathrm{crit}}_{Q,W,\mathscr K}=\bigoplus_{\mathbf d}\ \bigoplus_{z\in S_{\mathbf d}}\ \bigoplus_{n\in\mathbb Z}H^{-n}_{G_{\mathbf d}}(X_{\mathbf d},K_{\mathbf d,z}).$$
The index $n$ is the intrinsic Borel–Moore index. For inputs in
$(\mathbf a,z_1)$ and $(\mathbf b,z_2)$, take their external product,
ordinary inverse image along $q$, identify the result with
$K_{E,z_1,z_2}[-2r]$ using the datum, and apply its proper coefficient
morphism. Here $r=-\chi_Q(\mathbf b,\mathbf a)$ and $p$ is proper by
[[lem-quiver-exact-sequence-correspondence-is-smooth-and-proper]]. The
product therefore has degree
$$\mathcal H^{\mathrm{crit}}_{n,\mathbf a,z_1}\otimes\mathcal H^{\mathrm{crit}}_{m,\mathbf b,z_2}\longrightarrow\mathcal H^{\mathrm{crit}}_{n+m-2\chi_Q(\mathbf b,\mathbf a),\mathbf a+\mathbf b,z_1+z_2}.$$
Trace additivity is
[[lem-quiver-potential-trace-is-additive-on-extensions]]. Coherent
presentation and frame operations use
[[def-intrinsic-quotient-stack-borel-moore-grading]]. Finite supported
inputs have finite supported products, so this algebraic direct sum
needs no completion. Dimension zero has its specified identity unit.

The standard rational coefficient datum EXISTS by
[[lem-standard-rational-quiver-vanishing-cycles-realize-critical-correspondences]].
For this datum write $\mathcal H^{\mathrm{crit}}_{Q,W}$ without an extra
choice. Explicitly, with $g=\dim G_{\mathbf d}$,
$$\mathcal H^{\mathrm{crit}}_{n,\mathbf d,z}=H^{-n-2g}_{G_{\mathbf d}}(X_{\mathbf d},D^{G_{\mathbf d}}\Phi_{\mathbf d,z}).$$
On a free frame quotient $X_U$ with $t=\dim U$, this is the stable value
$H^{-n-2t}(X_U,D\Phi_U)$ degree by degree. It is NOT the unshifted
variety-normalized equivariant group. On smooth charts the standard
constant-input duality identifies $D\Phi=\omega\otimes\Phi$; the
intrinsic shift remains. Equivalently one may take the degreewise dual
of normalized compact-support cohomology, justified on finite models
and then stabilized; no unrestricted dual of the whole graded sum is
used. All these coefficients retain monodromy. For $W=0$ this is the
ordinary intrinsic rational CoHA of
[[def-untwisted-quiver-cohomological-hall-algebra]], with the same
proper/smooth maps and degree convention.
thm-critical-quiver-coha-associative-und:
## Statement

Assume AC. For every finite complex quiver $Q$, every finite potential $W$
and every coherent datum $\mathscr K$ of
[[def-quiver-potential-and-monodromic-vanishing-cycle-data]], the critical
CoHA of [[def-critical-quiver-coha-from-vanishing-cycle-data]] is associative
and unital. In particular its standard rational monodromic vanishing-cycle
instance exists and is associative and unital, for arbitrary critical values,
loops and multiple arrows. For $W=0$ it recovers the ordinary intrinsic
rational quiver CoHA with the same multiplication and grading.
